plotting_plan.title: Progressive Baseline Ladder Architecture
plotting_plan.objective: Block diagram showing the progressive baseline ladder (B0-B5) built on SegFormer-B2 with SharedFPN. Show how auxiliary heads (skeleton DT, endpoints, junctions, width) are incrementally added. Include the three post-hoc graph extraction methods (A: skeleton, B: DT ridge, C: DT peak).

plotting_plan.title: Multi-Seed Baseline Comparison
plotting_plan.objective: Grouped bar chart with error bars (3 seeds) comparing B0, B1a (clDice), and B2_best (skeleton DT) on mIoU_fg. Annotate paired t-test p-values above each comparison. Show that single-seed results (diamond markers) can be misleading vs multi-seed means.

plotting_plan.title: Three Overturned Single-Seed Claims
plotting_plan.objective: Visual comparison (Dumbbell Chart, 3-panel) showing how single-seed conclusions were overturned by multi-seed validation: (a) B2 '+1%' -> +0.5% ns, (b) B1a '-1.6%' -> +0.2% ns, (c) MixStyle '+52%' OOD -> ~0% ns. Each panel shows individual seed values connected to the mean, with p-values annotated.

plotting_plan.title: Post-Hoc Graph Extraction Quality
plotting_plan.objective: Grouped bar chart comparing Methods A, B, C on edge F1 at three tolerance tiers (strict @5px, relaxed @10px, lenient @15px) for B2_best model. Include box plot overlays showing per-image distribution (emphasize that median = 0 for most methods).

plotting_plan.title: Domain Generalization Multi-Seed Results
plotting_plan.objective: Bar chart with error bars (3 seeds) showing DamSegment mIoU_fg (left cluster) and s2ds mIoU_fg (right cluster) for ERM, CORAL, DANN, MixStyle. Annotate domain gap (~55%) and statistical equivalence (p=0.878). Include a horizontal dashed line at the ERM mean for visual reference.

plotting_plan.title: Direct Graph Prediction: Overfit vs Full Training
plotting_plan.objective: Paired bar chart comparing P3 overfit results (16 images) vs full training (1275 images) on node F1@5px, edge_gt F1@10px, and edge F1@10px. Show the dramatic gap between overfit success and full-train failure, illustrating the auto-label ceiling effect.

introduction_strategy.hook_hypothesis: Automated crack and spalling detection from inspection images is critical for infrastructure safety, and deep learning segmentation models have become the standard approach.
introduction_strategy.problem_gap_hypothesis: Despite widespread adoption of auxiliary morphological supervision (topology-preserving losses, skeleton heads, keypoint detection) to improve crack segmentation quality, the effectiveness of these methods has not been rigorously validated with multi-seed experiments. Similarly, standard domain generalization methods have not been systematically evaluated for cross-site concrete defect segmentation under realistic single-source conditions.

Search for published surveys on structural health monitoring using computer vision and deep learning
Identify foundational papers on semantic segmentation architectures (SegFormer, DeepLabV3+, U-Net) applied to infrastructure inspection
Find papers establishing the importance of cross-site generalization in structural inspection and infrastructure monitoring
Search for papers discussing reproducibility and seed sensitivity in deep learning for civil engineering applications

related_work_strategy.overview: Investigate three methodology clusters that our systematic study evaluates: topology-aware segmentation losses, morphological graph extraction from crack images, and domain generalization for infrastructure defect detection.

subsections.methodology_cluster: Topology-aware auxiliary losses (clDice, persistent homology, connectivity losses)
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Find recent papers (2020-2026) that apply topology-preserving losses to crack or thin-structure segmentation. Identify which ones report multi-seed results vs single-seed.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: These methods are typically validated with single random seeds, making their reported improvements potentially attributable to seed variance rather than genuine methodological gains.

subsections.bridge_to_our_method: Our multi-seed evaluation reveals that clDice does not significantly improve (or harm) crack segmentation when properly validated with multiple seeds.

subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Find papers on crack skeleton extraction, morphological analysis, and graph-based crack representation from 2019-2026. Identify what graph metrics are used to evaluate structural quality.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: Skeleton-based auxiliary supervision is assumed to improve downstream graph extraction quality, but this assumption has not been empirically tested with proper controls and statistical validation.

subsections.bridge_to_our_method: Our study shows that skeleton DT supervision does not significantly improve segmentation or post-hoc graph extraction quality, and that direct neural graph prediction is limited by auto-label quality.

subsections.methodology_cluster: Domain generalization methods (CORAL, DANN, MixStyle, data augmentation) for cross-site defect detection
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Find papers applying domain generalization or domain adaptation to concrete defect detection or structural health monitoring from 2020-2026. Identify whether multi-site evaluation is standard practice.

subsections.bridge_to_our_method: Our multi-seed evaluation reveals that all three standard DG methods are statistically equivalent to ERM baseline, demonstrating that pseudo-domain strategies are insufficient for bridging real cross-site gaps.

content_bullets: State the problem: auxiliary morphological supervision is widely used to improve crack segmentation but has not been rigorously validated with multi-seed experiments.

Describe the study: systematic evaluation of a progressive baseline ladder (B0-B5) on SegFormer-B2, three post-hoc graph extraction methods, direct neural graph prediction, and three standard DG methods, all on concrete dam inspection imagery.
Present the central negative finding: three single-seed conclusions were overturned by multi-seed validation (B2 skeleton DT '+1%', B1a clDice '-1.6%', MixStyle '+52%' OOD).
State the contribution: a rigorous experimental methodology with go/no-go gates and multi-tier graph evaluation that reveals the fragility of single-seed conclusions in this domain.
Describe the SegFormer-B2 backbone with MIT encoder and MLP decoder, operating at 512x512 resolution.
Detail the SharedFPN architecture that enables multi-task head attachment.
Specify the B0 mask-only baseline: weighted CE loss [0.2, 2.0, 3.0] + Dice loss for 3-class segmentation (background, crack, spalling).
Training protocol: 100 epochs, differential LR (encoder 6e-5, heads 6e-4), GroupNorm (batch=4), mixed precision.

content_bullets: B1a: B0 + soft clDice loss on crack class (weight=0.15, activated at epoch 40 with 5-epoch ramp). Define the clDice formulation as soft skeleton recall times soft skeleton precision.
B2: B0 + skeleton distance transform regression head (MSE loss, weight=10, unmasked DT target). Describe the normalized DT computation from crack masks.
B3: B0 + endpoint and junction detection heads (BCE with high pos_weight for extreme class imbalance, plus keypoint Dice loss).
B5: B0 + full joint supervision (skeleton DT + keypoints + width regression). Explain the progressive loss activation schedule.
Emphasize: each baseline adds one supervision type incrementally, with identical training budget (100 epochs) for fair comparison.

content_bullets: Method A (skeleton extraction): skeletonize predicted crack mask, extract endpoints (degree-1) and junctions (degree>=3) as nodes, connected skeleton segments as edges.
Method B (DT ridge detection): find ridges in predicted distance transform map above threshold, extract graph from ridge skeleton.
Method C (DT peak detection): find local maxima in predicted DT map, connect peaks by proximity to form graph edges.
Define the multi-tier evaluation protocol: strict (@5px), relaxed (@10px), lenient (@15px) tolerance for node matching, with corresponding edge F1 metrics.

research paper or technical report introducing 'graph edit distance'

content_bullets: Describe pseudo-domain construction: DamSegment images split into Easy/Medium/Hard tiers based on defect difficulty, used as proxy source domains.
CORAL: covariance alignment loss between pseudo-domain feature distributions, applied at encoder stage 2.
DANN: gradient reversal layer + domain discriminator MLP, with GRL alpha scheduling from 0 to 1 over training.
MixStyle: Beta-distributed mixing of instance normalization statistics, applied as forward hooks on encoder stages 0-1.
Multi-seed protocol: 3 seeds (42, 123, 7) x 4 methods = 12 runs, with paired t-test for significance.

content_bullets: DamSegment: 1500 concrete dam inspection images, 640x640, resized to 512x512, train/val split 1275/225. RGB-encoded masks with 3 classes. Class imbalance: background 96.6%, crack 2.2%, spalling 1.2%.
s2ds: 743 images at 512x512, out-of-distribution test set from different inspection sites. Used only for cross-domain evaluation, never for training.
Describe the data split strategy and leakage prevention (perceptual hash dedup).

content_bullets: Segmentation: mIoU_fg (mean IoU over foreground classes), per-class IoU, BF1 (boundary F1).
Graph: endpoint F1, junction F1, edge F1 at three tolerance tiers, graph edit distance, path continuity, width MAE.
Instance: spalling instance P/R/F1 via connected components + Hungarian matching at IoU threshold 0.5.
Cross-domain: domain gap defined as DamSegment mIoU_fg minus s2ds mIoU_fg.
Statistical tests: paired t-test for multi-seed comparisons, Wilcoxon signed-rank for paired per-image comparisons, TOST equivalence test with margin +/-1% mIoU.

subsections.subsection_title: 5.1 Auxiliary Supervision Does Not Improve Segmentation
content_bullets: Present Table 1b: B0 vs B1a vs B2_best multi-seed results. B1a: +0.2%+/-0.9% (p=0.822), B2_best: +0.5%+/-0.3% (p=0.145). Neither significant.
Present single-seed ladder (Table 1) for context: B3 -0.5%, B5 -2.7% vs B0.
Discuss the DT weight sweep (Table 2): apparent optimum at w=10 vanishes under multi-seed.
Discuss B1a variance: std=0.015 vs B0's 0.008, suggesting clDice makes training less stable.
Reference fig_multiseed_baseline_comparison.
Present Table 3: edge F1 at three tiers for Method A. Median edge F1 = 0 across all methods.
Present Table 4: B0 vs B2_best on graph metrics. All Wilcoxon p > 0.23, skeleton supervision does not help graph extraction.
Compare Methods A, B, C: skeleton extraction (A) outperforms DT-based methods (B, C).
Discuss spalling instance baseline (Table 5): post-hoc CC achieves micro F1 = 0.567 without any learned instance head.
Reference fig_graph_extraction_edge_f1.

subsections.subsection_title: 5.3 Direct Graph Prediction Hits the Auto-Label Ceiling
content_bullets: Present P3 overfit results (Table 6): all gates pass (node F1=0.934, edge_gt F1=0.917).
Present P3 full train results (Table 7): gates fail (node F1=0.30, edge F1=0.195).
P3h hybrid analysis (Table 8): edge classifier generalizes well (edge_gt F1 0.654 vs 0.454), confirming node localization as the bottleneck.
Root cause: auto-generated labels from mask-to-graph pipeline limit what the model can learn. Gold standard annotations are needed.
Reference fig_p3_overfit_vs_full.

subsections.subsection_title: 5.4 Domain Generalization Methods Are Ineffective Under Pseudo-Domains
content_bullets: Present Table 10: multi-seed DG results. All four methods statistically equivalent (MixStyle vs ERM p=0.878).
Present Table 9: cross-domain baseline showing ~55% domain gap (DamSegment to s2ds).
Discuss why pseudo-domains fail: difficulty-based tiers do not capture genuine cross-site distribution shifts (different sensors, environments, surface textures).
Reference fig_dg_multiseed_domain_gap.
Present the three overturned claims side-by-side: B2 '+1%', B1a '-1.6%', MixStyle '+52%'.
Quantify the magnitude of seed variance relative to reported effect sizes.
Discuss implications for the broader crack segmentation literature where single-seed evaluation is standard practice.
Argue that multi-seed validation should be a minimum requirement for claims of improvement.
Reference fig_single_vs_multiseed_overturned.

content_bullets: Summarize the central negative finding: no auxiliary morphological supervision significantly improves crack segmentation when properly validated with multiple seeds.
Summarize the DG negative finding: standard DG methods do not reduce cross-site domain gap under pseudo-domain single-source training.
Highlight the methodological contribution: three cases of misleading single-seed results overturned by multi-seed validation.
Discuss the auto-label ceiling as a fundamental limitation for neural graph prediction without gold standard annotations.
State future work: gold standard graph annotations, true multi-source domain generalization with multiple inspection sites, and learned instance segmentation heads.
Provide practical recommendations: use B0 mask-only baseline as the default (simplest, equally effective), invest in multi-site data collection rather than DG method development.
